newsitem.title: USA: Birds' descent from dinosaurs in doubt.
newsitem.headline: Birds' descent from dinosaurs in doubt.

text.p: Scientists have unearthed new evidence challenging the theory that birds descend from dinosaurs, according to findings reported on Thursday in the journal Science.
Studying bird fossils found in northeastern China, a team of researchers wrote that birds may have originated much earlier than thought.
The fossils date to the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous periods, about 140 million years ago.

They said that this suggested the ancestor of modern birds first arose during the Middle Jurassic period or earlier. Some scientists believe dinosaurs thought to be most like modern birds date to the Late Cretaceous period, about 76 million years later than the fossil birds.

The scientists, including Larry Martin of Kansas University, Zhonghe Zhou, a student of Martin's, Lianhai Hou of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Alan Feduccia of the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill, wrote that the fossils point to a separation of birds into two distinct lines.
They said one line gave rise to modern birds and the other prospered and diversified until they became extinct along with dinosaurs at the end of the Cretaceous period.
"This exacebates one of the most obvious conundrums facing the theory of dinosaurian origin of birds," the scientists wrote.

"The discovery that the line leading to modern birds coexisted almost from the earliest occurence of birds in the fossil record with an archaic group of now extinct birds is the most important discovery in fossil birds since Archaeopterys," Martin said.
Archaeopterys was a toothed bird and the first bird discovered to have lived during the Jurassic period.
The researchers based their findings on three fossil birds excavated during digging in the Jurassic-Cretaceous deposits of northeastern China.
They were named Confuciusornis, Liaoningornis and Chaoyangla.
